title: Dior Sauvage Alternatives From Real Fragrance Houses, Not Clones
summary: Five fragrances from Creed, YSL, Parfums de Marly, Prada and Versace that share at least one official note with Dior Sauvage Eau de Parfum, each set against Dior's own note list. It also explains how an alternative differs from a clone and compares Sauvage with Creed Aventus note by note.
tags: dior sauvage alternative not a clone
author: Jeff Theefs
image_alt: Halved bergamot, cracked Sichuan peppercorns and two star anise pods on a dark slate board beside three generic unbranded clear-glass 5 ml atomizers and a folded forest-green linen napkin on a cream travertine ledge in soft dawn light
seo_title: Dior Sauvage Alternatives From Real Houses | Base Note
seo_description: Five fragrances that share official notes with Dior Sauvage Eau de Parfum, from Creed, YSL, Parfums de Marly, Prada and Versace. Alternatives, not clones.

fig-01.alt: Simple illustration of a fragrance as a recipe of smells: a clone tries to copy the whole recipe, while an alternative is a different recipe that uses some of the same smells, shown as two matching circled icons
fig-01.caption: A clone tries to copy another fragrance's recipe. An alternative is its own recipe that shares a few of the same smells.

fig-02.alt: Note-overlap map with Dior Sauvage Eau de Parfum in the centre and five alternatives around it, each labelled with the official notes it shares with Sauvage and one way it differs: Creed Green Irish Tweed, YSL Y Eau de Parfum Intense, Parfums de Marly Perseus, Prada Paradigme and Versace Eros Eau de Parfum
fig-02.caption: Each alternative is linked to Sauvage only by notes named on both manufacturers' pages; the layout is not a ranking.

fig-03.alt: Close-up of cracked Sichuan peppercorns with split reddish husks and a curl of bergamot peel resting on cream travertine stone

fig-04.alt: Six generic unbranded clear-glass 5 ml atomizers in a row on cream travertine, one set slightly apart from the other five, with a forest-green linen strip along the lower edge
